we describe a new syndrome of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia in adults that is not due to insulinoma and that is independent of mutations in the Kir6.2 or SUR1 genes.
we describe five adult patients with neuroglycogenic symptoms from hyperinsulinemia and negative 72 h fasts.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the five cases reported herein represent a new syndrome of hyperinsu-linemic hypoglycemias in adult humans.
this syndrome is a novel syndrome of noninsulinoma pancreetogenous hypoglycaemia in adults.

the syndrome is characterized by the following: 1) postprandial hyperinsulinemic neuroglycopenia with negative 72-h fasting test; 2) no evidence of an insulinoma; 3) diffuse beta-cell hyperplasia with islet hypertrophy; 4) no mutation in Kir6. or SUR1 gene; and 5) response to partial pancreatectomies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have described a new syndrome of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia in adults, which we call non-insulinoma pancreatogenic hypoglycaemic (NIPHS).

this syndrome, noninsulinoma pancreetogenous hypoglycaemia, should be considered in the differential diagnosis of adults with neuroglyopenic episodes after meal ingestion and normal 72-h fasting glucose levels.
the clinical features and responses of these adults to dynamic testing in hyperinsulinemic-hypoglycemia are consistent with a new syndrome of noninsulinoma pancreetogenous hypoglycemias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of insulinoma in adults should not be made solely on the basis of a positive 72-h fast.
there are patients who have hyperinsulinemic postprandial syndrome and who don't have insulinoma.
the differential diagnosis of adult hyperinsulinemic postprandial hyperglycemia includes a syndrome of diffuse beta-cell hyperplasia.
